rationale:
bugs_open/376. `vertical-exemplar-researcher` is hop two of every greenfield build. It crawls three exemplar sites in a strictly linear chain (select_exemplars -> crawl_1 -> format_1 -> crawl_2 -> format_2 -> crawl_3 -> format_3 -> synthesise -> write_landscape_spec -> create_next_item) with NO error_step on any crawl step [re-confirmed on the live row 2026-08-25]. Two upstream outcomes need two different guards, and the obvious fix would have made things WORSE:

(a) A crawl ERRORS (Firecrawl refuses the host). Today the stage dies, the crawls that succeeded are discarded, and create_next_item never runs, so the build stops with nothing to say why. [MEASURED 2026-08-23, garden-tools.uk] thespruce.com was drawn in 4 of 5 selections and refused every time; three consecutive attempts died at whichever crawl drew it. Severity HIGH: create_next_item is the LAST step, so the whole hop is lost.

(b) A crawl SUCCEEDS and delivers NOTHING. [MEASURED 2026-08-25 10:52:41Z, homegarden.uk canary, orchestration 5937f08b] crawl_exemplar_3 (which.co.uk/reviews/home-and-garden) returned success:true; format_exemplar_3 returned {sources:[], source_count:0, content_quality:'none'}; the workflow moved to synthesise anyway and wrote a vertical landscape from two exemplars while every status said three. Silent, and it has happened on a live build.

So a floor evaluated on STEP SUCCESS is blind to (b) — which.co.uk would count toward it — and in the degenerate case the estate would write a landscape from NO research with every step green, strictly worse than today's loud stop. The floor must be evaluated on CONTENT: formatted_N.source_count.

The design (bug §11) was verified against the code that executes it, not inferred from config: (1) format_crawl_for_analysis returns a graceful {source_count:0, content_quality:'none'} with a NIL error when it finds no pages, and ExtractNestedField returns nil for a MISSING crawl_N exactly as for an empty one — so routing a refused crawl to ITS OWN format step makes (a) collapse into (b) and lets one floor count both; routing to the NEXT crawl would leave formatted_N absent, which synthesise interpolates as '<no value>' and the floor cannot count. (2) routeToErrorStepOrFail (coordinator.go:3916) honours step-level error_step first, config-level second; both live. (3) conditional_branch's evaluator (conditional_branch_action.go:144-186) splits on ' OR ' first, then ' AND ', and cleanExpressionPart STRIPS parentheses — so the 2-of-3 floor is written bracket-free, 'A AND B OR A AND C OR B AND C', which parses as (A^B) v (A^C) v (B^C); brackets would silently change the meaning (LANDMINE filed 2026-08-25). fail_on_non_numeric:true is load-bearing: without it a source_count that fails to resolve evaluates false and routes to the failure arm silently, so a broken instrument would read as a genuine shortfall. (4) __step_error is a single key overwritten on every routed failure (bugs_open/243), so it is NOT the floor's input; source_count is per-exemplar and cannot be clobbered.

Below the floor the run must fail LOUDLY and NAMED: a query_database step composes the failure text WITH the three counts (orchestration_states is reaped within ~25h, so the counts must reach a durable row), then fail_workflow ends the run with a FAILURE verdict; the handler saga marks the needs_vertical_research item failed with that text in `error`, and create_next_item never runs.

Rehearsed 2026-08-25 against the live row inside a rolled-back transaction: drift guard passed, edit applied, verify block passed (3 error_steps, floor wired, 0 dangling edges, 15 steps), and the ROLLBACK file restores the 12-step chain in the same transaction. Live row untouched (applied=false, 12 steps).

Config only; no ordering constraint claimed (owner ruling 2026-07-29). No new domain is dispatched on the greenfield route until this ships (hop two is a 4-in-5 kill on the one vertical measured).

plan.summary: One migration on the live vertical-exemplar-researcher row: (1) step-level error_step on each of the three crawl steps pointing at that exemplar's OWN format step, so a refused crawl formats to source_count 0 and is counted rather than skipped; (2) a bracket-free 2-of-3 floor on formatted_N.source_count between format_exemplar_3 and synthesise, with fail_on_non_numeric so a broken count errors loudly; (3) below the floor, a query_database step records the three counts in the failure text and fail_workflow ends the run with a FAILURE verdict, so the work item's error names the cause and create_next_item never runs. A ROLLBACK sidecar reverses exactly the seven keys touched.

edits.rationale: Tell the migration runner when this is already applied, keyed on the step this file adds, so a re-run reports LIKELY ALREADY APPLIED instead of failing inside the edit.

edits.symbol: snapshot + DO $edit$ (drift guard, three error_steps, the floor, the record + fail steps)
edits.rationale: Guard and edit in ONE block so they read the same row. The drift guard asserts the exact 12-step shape §11 was verified against (crawl action, no existing error_step at either level, format output_field, format_3 -> synthesise, no step this file adds already present) and asserts on the literal condition that it carries no parentheses. Then: crawl_N.error_step = format_exemplar_N at STEP level; format_exemplar_3.next_step = check_exemplar_floor; three new steps.

Post-conditions as RAISEs (a SELECT cannot stop a COMMIT): the three error_steps set, the floor wiring, fail_on_non_numeric true, no parentheses reached the stored condition, 0 dangling edges (546's post-condition), and synthesise still consumes formatted_1..3.

The inverse edit, not a snapshot restore (a snapshot restore would discard anything another lane changed on the row since). Probe-guarded on the presence of check_exemplar_floor; removes the three error_steps and the three added steps, restores format_exemplar_3.next_step = synthesise, and RAISEs unless exactly 12 steps remain. Rehearsed apply-then-rollback in one transaction.

plan.risks: 1) EXPECTED OBJECTION — 'the floor lets a build proceed on 2 of 3 exemplars; why not 3?' Answer: research is N-of-3, not a transaction (bug §5 candidate 1); the synthesis prompt already reads formatted_N as free text and a 'none' exemplar reads as one with no content; 2-of-3 is the floor below which a landscape is fiction. 3-of-3 would reinstate today's 4-in-5 kill on the one vertical measured. 2) A format_exemplar_N step that itself ERRORS (not the empty case — a DB fallback failure) still has no error_step; that is the pre-existing rarer path and is deliberately out of scope (§11e). A reviewer may ask for it; the answer is that it needs its own floor input and is a separate change. 3) The reason text is composed by query_database with $1::text casts on values that arrive from collected_data as JSON numbers; the rehearsal exercised the DDL, not a live run through record_exemplar_floor. The three post-apply tests in the file header are REQUIRED before the bug closes (refused host, succeeds-but-empty host, induced below-floor run). 4) Parenthesis trap: a later editor 'tidying' the condition with brackets silently changes the meaning; the verify block and a LANDMINE entry both say so, and the migration RAISEs if the stored literal ever carries one. 5) Config-level vs step-level error_step both work (measured); this file uses step level and its drift guard checks BOTH levels for a pre-existing value so a config-level twin cannot be silently duplicated. 6) Interaction with the selection candidate (exclude refused hosts, §5 cand 2): independent — this changes what happens when a choice fails, that changes what is chosen.
